about: Teaching-style profile measured from the 4 most recent long videos and the 10 most recent Shorts of a table tennis coaching channel. The reference files stay in backend/data/style_ref/ (git-ignored, never shown in the app). Only structure, pacing and teaching approach are recorded here, in our own words.

long_form: numbered keys, one at a time
structure.notes: Every phase is shown on the real motion first, then frozen on its key frame while the cue is on screen. Comparisons stack two players and mark the good version with a tick and the mistake with a cross.

pacing.notes: Teaching Shorts run 10-15 s: about 2 s of hook, 2.5-3 s per phase, 1.5-2.5 s of recap. Long videos cut every ~5-6 s and spend about half their runtime on held frames of about 1 s each, with ~1 s slow-motion stretches.

card_layout.header: Persistent two-line title in the top-left: the stroke on line one, a short hook in the accent colour on line two.
card_layout.cue: Bottom third, under the footage: the phase cue in large condensed caps in that phase's own colour, with one short plain sentence under it.
card_layout.numbering: Small numbered chips (01, 02, 03) tie each cue to its place in the sequence.
card_layout.highlight: The body part or bat path that the cue is about is drawn in the cue's colour (glow, arrow or trail), so colour links words to motion.
card_layout.recap: All cue words on one line joined with '+', each in its colour, plus one summary line.
card_layout.background: Dark navy behind the footage; text never covers the player.

phase_naming.pattern: Short imperative cue: an action plus a direction or body part, in caps (for example our own LOAD LOW, LIFT THROUGH, END HIGH).
phase_naming.explanation_line: One short sentence (about 4-7 words) saying what to look for.

principles: Number the keys and keep them to three or four.
Pair every cue with the reason it works.
Use concrete body landmarks: foot angle, knee bend, where the bat starts, shoulder turn.
Explain the chain: legs, then hips, then chest, then arm, with the wrist last.
Stay relaxed and accelerate into contact; tense only at the ball.
Name one common mistake and its fix.
Finish with a simple practice drill the player can do alone.
coaching.tone: Direct, second person, short sentences, no filler.

render.notes: TTSkill's own palette (ball orange first); the references' colours and fonts are not used.
